reuse.why: All bulk actions reuse getBulkBudgetCategories, but fixed-tag detection bypasses extractTagsFromText and the new spending action repeats the sign conversion in averageToBudget.

duplication.why: Category exclusions remain centralized, while tag recognition and income-versus-expense sign handling acquire separate implementations.

placement.why: Budget selection and mutation stay in the established server budget layer, although tag parsing belongs in the existing shared tags module.

scope.why: The changes address the requested budget actions, apart from an unrelated import reorder in schedules/app.ts.

maintainability.why: Centralized exclusions and conventional method registration are maintainable, but parallel tag and sign rules should be consolidated before merging.

bypasses_abstraction.where: actions.ts:getBulkBudgetCategories uses split/includes instead of shared/tags.ts:extractTagsFromText; setLastMonthSpending independently implements the sign decision already represented by averageToBudget.

disguised_duplication.where: setLastMonthSpending reverses the income/expense conditional and combines negation with clamping, reshaping averageToBudget's existing sign decision; fixed-tag recognition replaces the shared tag parser with whitespace splitting.

abstraction_drift.where: getBulkBudgetCategories renames the existing includeHidden parameter and adds one fixed-group rejection branch; its template exclusion is centralized in SQL, while tag parsing and the new spending sign conversion bypass existing helpers.
